prompt:
You are an industrial process monitoring engineer. The Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) shows an abnormal episode. Your task: identify the root cause.

Dataset: Tennessee Eastman Process simulation. Columns: XMEAS_1..41 process measurements, XMV_1..11 manipulator variables (Downs-Vogel standard mapping). Sampling: 3 minutes. Fault onset: sample 161 of 960.
Blind statistical monitoring results (computed from the data):
- Per-column max |z|-score (top columns): XMEAS_6 max|z|=4.26 (0.3% beyond 3σ); XMV_8 max|z|=3.88 (0.2% beyond 3σ); XMEAS_15 max|z|=3.88 (0.2% beyond 3σ); XMEAS_4 max|z|=3.77 (0.2% beyond 3σ); XMEAS_30 max|z|=3.72 (0.4% beyond 3σ); XMV_6 max|z|=3.63 (0.2% beyond 3σ)
- Strongest cross-domain correlations: XMEAS_12 ~ XMV_7: r=1.000; XMEAS_15 ~ XMV_8: r=1.000; XMEAS_17 ~ XMV_11: r=-0.999; XMEAS_7 ~ XMEAS_13: r=0.998; XMEAS_1 ~ XMV_3: r=0.997; XMEAS_19 ~ XMV_9: r=0.988

Process description: Tennessee Eastman 化工过程：反应器-冷凝器-气液分离器-汽提塔+循环压缩机。XMEAS_1..41 过程测量、XMV_1..11 操纵变量。3分钟采样，第161样本（8h）起进入异常工况。本记录为文献公认统计弱签名场景，全列谱偏离幅度小，需依赖位点结构与排除法判别。

Task: identify the root cause of this abnormal episode. Output STRICT JSON only (no markdown, no extra text): {"top3": ["<root cause id/name>", ...], "reasoning": "<2-3 sentences>"} where top3 is your ranked list of up to 3 candidate root causes.

top3: IDV(3) - Step change in D feed temperature (stream 2 feed temperature step)
IDV(9) - Random variation of D feed temperature (stream 2)
IDV(2) - Step change in B feed composition (A/C feed ratio held constant)
answer.reasoning: All columns deviate only weakly (max|z|<=4.3, <0.5% of samples beyond 3-sigma) after the step-like onset at sample 161, and the excursions concentrate in the feed-rate loops (XMEAS_6, XMEAS_4, XMV_6), the stripper level/product-flow control pair (XMEAS_15 ~ XMV_8, r=1.000), and product composition (XMEAS_30), while reactor temperature/pressure and both cooling-water circuits (XMV_10/XMV_11, XMEAS_21/XMEAS_22) remain quiet, which excludes cooling-water faults (IDV 4/5/11/12/14/15) and reaction-kinetics drift (IDV 13). The remaining signature — a small feed/product-composition disturbance propagating into feed and stripper inventory loops with no directly instrumented feed-temperature measurement — matches the literature's statistically weakest TEP scenario: a step change in the D feed (stream 2) temperature, i.e. IDV(3), with IDV(9) as the same-site random-variation alternative.
